items.name: CaptureLocations
items.summary: CaptureLocations is a low level representation of the raw offsets of each submatch.

methods.name: get
methods.signature: fn get(&self, i: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)>
methods.summary: Returns the start and end positions of the Nth capture group.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the total number of capturing groups.

items.name: CaptureMatches
items.summary: An iterator that yields all non-overlapping capture groups matching a particular regular expression.

items.name: Captures
items.summary: Captures represents a group of captured byte strings for a single match.

methods.name: get
methods.summary: Returns the match associated with the capture group at index `i`. If `i` does not correspond to a capture group, or if the capture group did not participate in the match, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: len
methods.summary: Returns the number of captured groups.

methods.name: name
methods.summary: Returns the match for the capture group named `name`. If `name` isn't a valid capture group or didn't match anything, then `None` is returned.

items.name: Match
items.summary: Match represents a single match of a regex in a subject string.

methods.name: as_bytes
methods.summary: Returns the matched portion of the subject string.

methods.name: end
methods.summary: Returns the ending byte offset of the match in the subject.

methods.name: start
methods.summary: Returns the starting byte offset of the match in the subject.

items.name: Matches
items.summary: An iterator over all non-overlapping matches for a particular subject string.

methods.name: as_str
methods.summary: Returns the original pattern string for this regex.

methods.name: capture_locations
methods.summary: Returns an empty set of capture locations that can be reused in multiple calls to `captures_read` or `captures_read_at`.

methods.name: capture_names
methods.summary: Returns a sequence of all capturing groups and their names, if present.

methods.name: captures
methods.summary: Returns the capture groups corresponding to the leftmost-first match in `subject`. Capture group `0` always corresponds to the entire match. If no match is found, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: captures_iter
methods.summary: Returns an iterator over all the non-overlapping capture groups matched in `subject`. This is operationally the same as `find_iter`, except it yields information about capturing group matches.

methods.name: captures_len
methods.summary: Returns the number of capturing groups in the pattern.

methods.name: captures_read
methods.signature: fn captures_read<'s>(&self, locs: &mut CaptureLocations, subject: &'s [u8]) -> Result<Option<Match<'s>>, Error>
methods.summary: This is like `captures`, but uses [`CaptureLocations`](struct.CaptureLocations.html) instead of [`Captures`](struct.Captures.html) in order to amortize allocations.

methods.name: captures_read_at
methods.signature: fn captures_read_at<'s>(&self, locs: &mut CaptureLocations, subject: &'s [u8], start: usize) -> Result<Option<Match<'s>>, Error>
methods.summary: Returns the same as `captures_read`, but starts the search at the given offset and populates the capture locations given.

methods.name: find
methods.summary: Returns the start and end byte range of the leftmost-first match in `subject`. If no match exists, then `None` is returned.

methods.name: find_at
methods.signature: fn find_at<'s>(&self, subject: &'s [u8], start: usize) -> Result<Option<Match<'s>>, Error>
methods.summary: Returns the same as find, but starts the search at the given offset.

methods.name: find_iter
methods.summary: Returns an iterator for each successive non-overlapping match in `subject`, returning the start and end byte indices with respect to `subject`.

methods.name: is_match
methods.summary: Returns true if and only if the regex matches the subject string given.

methods.name: is_match_at
methods.signature: fn is_match_at(&self, subject: &[u8], start: usize) -> Result<bool, Error>
methods.summary: Returns the same as is_match, but starts the search at the given offset.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Compiles a regular expression using the default configuration.

items.name: RegexBuilder
items.summary: A builder for configuring the compilation of a PCRE2 regex.

methods.name: build
methods.summary: Compile the given pattern into a PCRE regex using the current configuration.

methods.name: caseless
methods.signature: fn caseless(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enables case insensitive matching.

methods.name: crlf
methods.signature: fn crlf(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable matching of CRLF as a line terminator.

methods.name: disable_utf_check
methods.summary: This is now deprecated and is a no-op.

methods.name: dotall
methods.signature: fn dotall(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enables "dot all" matching.

methods.name: extended
methods.signature: fn extended(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable "extended" mode in the pattern, where whitespace is ignored.

methods.name: jit
methods.signature: fn jit(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable PCRE2's JIT and return an error if it's not available.

methods.name: jit_if_available
methods.signature: fn jit_if_available(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable PCRE2's JIT if it's available.

methods.name: max_jit_stack_size
methods.signature: fn max_jit_stack_size(&mut self, bytes: Option<usize>) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Set the maximum size of PCRE2's JIT stack, in bytes. If the JIT is not enabled, then this has no effect.

methods.name: multi_line
methods.signature: fn multi_line(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable multiline matching mode.

methods.name: new
methods.summary: Create a new builder with a default configuration.

methods.name: ucp
methods.signature: fn ucp(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable Unicode matching mode.

methods.name: utf
methods.signature: fn utf(&mut self, yes: bool) -> &mut RegexBuilder
methods.summary: Enable UTF matching mode.
